key_insight: Wear-resistant coatings for ventilation mill components are evaluated by linking microstructure, composition and hardness to abrasive-wear performance.
engineering_relevance: Coating selection could extend component service life in thermal power plant mills exposed to high temperatures and fast particle flows with sand concentrations up to 40%.
method: Use CFD to identify critical wear zones.
Evaluate manual metal arc welding, HVOF spraying and plasma welding with different filler compositions.
Characterize coatings using SEM–EDS, cross-sectional hardness measurements and controlled sandblasting tests.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental abrasion testing and coating characterization but gives no numerical wear reductions or best-performing coating.
watch_item: Laboratory sandblasting performance needs validation under combined thermal and abrasive conditions in operating mills.
paper_title: Analysis of Wear-Resistant Coating Technologies for Extending the Service Life of Ventilation Mill Components
